evidence_note: On the plant-earlier side, larger lead before bee detection predicts lower natural seed set at all three sites.

Early-to-late rank is weakly negative for initial fruit set (rho=-0.316) but strongly positive for final fruit set/intact fruit number (rho=+0.800), so the downstream predator stage reorients the timing signal.
Total-egg peak z=-1.10 sigma=0.92 shifts to active-egg peak z=-0.61 sigma=0.66; source fitness equation propagates the filtered window to final intact reproduction.

Early ecotype has longer flowering-to-egg interval (11.50 vs 5.72 d) and higher dehiscence-before-larval-completion rate (34% vs 4%); ecotype-level descriptive alignment, not individual-level pairing.
Synchrony predicts more predation in 2008 but less in 2009 as phase safety margin changes from -11.3 to +0.3 d.
Flowering date predicts oviposition exposure, but flowering/isolation/fruit number do not predict realized larval number (n=359; model R2=0.000).
Host stage and temperature alter larval performance, but mature-seedpod escape depends only on host species identity.
Across 21 years, the changing flowering-date–seed-predation covariance does not explain flowering-time selection (estimate=-0.033; 95% CI -0.101 to +0.037).
Redundancy is available only when partner activity overlaps flower receptivity; July 1998 moth cohort gap gives 0% open fruit set despite broader pollinator community.
Temporal escape and predator satiation produce nearly identical whole-season infestation (29% vs 30%) and no flowering-type effect on annual reproduction.
Egg density falls at pod maturation rather than tracking peak seed availability; final annual seed predation remains low relative to potential.
Final relative reproductive success declines with flowering onset in both years, although fruit-set and secondary-predation components differ between years.
Experimental shift across the host tissue window carries strongly to final reproductive fate: complete gall induction that destroys seed production falls from 80.9% before 15 June to 8.8% after.

Early flowers on multi-flowered plants attract more oviposition and experience higher relative seed predation, yet multi-flowered plants have greater annual seed output than single-flowered plants at all altitudes (later restatement: ~80-140% higher). The interaction-timing cost is buffered at whole-plant annual fitness.

Pollinator visitation declines >5-fold from week 1 to week 4, but the source reports no significant seed-set difference across four flowering weeks (F(3,36)=1.01). Later weeks contain a higher proportion of more-effective bumblebee visits, countering the visitation decline. The frozen week-1 minus week-4 SMD remains positive (g=+0.3815), but the source-level timing signal is biologically buffered before net seed set rather than classified as exact preservation.

In 2007, early low-visit plots precede late-July worker emergence and the middle window has high bumblebee visitation; intact mature seed set is higher in the high-service middle window at both HIS (g=+0.8518) and GOS (g=+1.0039), retained as one programme cluster.

Peak flowers had 7.5% legitimate oil-bee visit marks versus 93.6% in the late window; naturally pollinated late-vs-peak final seed-set log-odds is +1.55 (SE=0.25), preserving the service-window ordering to final reproduction.

Yellow-trap adult occurrence is aligned to experimentally identified susceptible ear emergence. Greater overlap and greater cumulative adult abundance during ear emergence both predict higher final yield loss across >400 susceptible cultivars over 2012-2013.

Later adult exposure from spike emergence toward anthesis produces less seed damage; susceptible spikes exposed two or more days after emergence have lower final yield loss than spikes exposed at emergence. Host resistance modifies magnitude but preserves timing direction.

Monarch herbivory is experimentally imposed at 60-, 74-, and 88-day host ages. Timing strongly changes downstream reproductive consequence: late-season herbivory has the strongest effect on viable-seed production, while early herbivory most affects plant size. Direct timing-to-final-fitness propagation; no natural adult-window comparator.

In Sinapis arvensis, herbivory timing strongly changes total seed mass, individual seed mass and germination, but integrated reproductive potential (seed number × germination) is unaffected by ontogeny among herbivory treatments (statistic=0.21,p=0.81). Source-demonstrated compensation makes this a buffered prospective timing signal.

In Brassica nigra under the same experimental architecture, final reproductive potential differs strongly with herbivory stage (ontogeny without controls statistic=41.2,p<0.001); vegetative/budding attack reduces final reproductive potential whereas flowering-stage attack is similar to control.

Tradescantia flowering onset is experimentally shifted across five weeks; focal-flower mature seed set increases with week (log-scale coefficient +0.41±0.15 SE,z=2.76,p=0.006). Pollinator composition and effectiveness change through time; source model explains 84% of among-treatment seed-set variation.

Asclepias flowering onset is experimentally shifted and mature seeds are counted after focal visits. Seed set per visit increases with later flowering; aggregated pollinator importance explains 80% of among-week variation and pollinator effectiveness included explains 90%.

Early array plants have high pollinator visitation and are not pollen limited but suffer severe frost and almost completely fail to reproduce; an abiotic downstream filter reverses the pollination-service expectation.

Late array plants receive low pollinator visitation, are strongly pollen limited, and have very low fruit/seed reproduction relative to controls, preserving the temporal pollination-service direction.

Across four experimental flowering weeks, pollinator access declines and mature seed set falls about 15%; phenology significantly affects seed set. Seed-set vs visitation rate is not significant (chi-square=3.14,p=0.08) and water has a stronger reproductive effect, so preservation does not imply pollinator mediation. Shares programme dependence with buffered IWE023.

Flowering abundance and key-pollinator visits independently define signed peak mismatch across an alpine community. Mismatch reaches seed-setting fitness, with pollinator-peaks-earlier significantly more detrimental than flower-peaks-earlier; flowering duration moderates the asymmetry. Registered as one programme link rather than species-level replications.

Nopporo 1999-2017 and the snow-removal experiment show the same direction: when Corydalis flowers before bumblebee emergence, increasing mismatch reduces natural seed set. Shares the long-term Corydalis dependence cluster with IWE001 and does not add an independent programme.

Early Pulsatilla flowers receive higher visitation despite lower total bee abundance; estimated total bee visits positively predict seed set. Open-pollinated seed set marginally declines with later bud opening (F=2.8,p=0.098), while hand-pollinated seed set does not; calendar date adds no explanatory power once total visits are included.

Without Phengaris alcon, selection favours earlier flowering; where the seed predator is present it preferentially attacks early plants and shifts final selection toward later flowering across 20 populations and two years.

Intact early-flower seeds have about twice the reproductive value of late-flower seeds, but late fruits escape seed predation; early and late reproductive values balance at ~63% predation and stronger population predation selects greater allocation to late flowers.

Flowering-time fitness differs between 2007 and 2008; late flowers can match early seed production when early ovule fertilization is prevented, pollen limitation is weak, and poor 2007 reproduction is mainly frost-related. Source-demonstrated resource reallocation/bet hedging buffers one stable timing-to-fitness direction.
